WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea: for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year." 2 Kings 17:4
Scripture says nothing of any answer from So. The king of Assyria shut Hoshea up in prison, besieged Samaria three years and took it. 2 Kings 17:4–6
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Israel's king turned from Assyria to Egypt: "he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt". 2 Kings 17:4
Israel was carried away into Assyria, to Halah, Habor by the river of Gozan, and the cities of the Medes. 2 Kings 17:6

DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
No regnal years. Who he was is disputed (see below), so no reign dates are given.
Shabaka (Sabaco), first king of the Ethiopian dynasty
James Ussher (1658); Ellicott's commentary; the Pulpit Commentary; T. Nicol (1915)

Ussher, citing Jerome's spelling of the name, took So to be "Sabacon the Ethiopian". Ellicott's commentary reads the Hebrew name as Seveh, the Egyptian Shabaka, "whom Sargon defeated at Raphia in 720 B.C."; the Pulpit Commentary says the Assyrians knew him as Sibakhi. Nicol, giving Shabaka 715–707 BC on Petrie's dates, supposes he could be called king while still regent. 2 Kings 17:4 [30][45][46][15]
Shabaka, as viceroy for his father
W. M. F. Petrie (1915)
Petrie writes that Shabaka was appointed viceroy of Egypt by his father Piankhy, and is the Assyrians' "Sibe, commander-in-chief of Muzri" and the Hebrews' "Sua or So". 2 Kings 17:4 [9]
Shabaka or his successor Sevechus; cannot yet be decided
C. F. Keil (1872), reporting Vitringa, Gesenius and Ewald for Sevechus

So is "one of the two Shebeks" of the Ethiopian dynasty; whether Sabako or his son Sevechus (held by Vitringa, Gesenius, Ewald) "cannot possibly be decided in the present state of Egyptological research". 2 Kings 17:4 [47]
Perhaps the Egyptian general Sib'e of Sargon's records
J. R. Lumby (1887)

Lumby thinks Shebek or Shebetek most probable, but notes the Egyptian general "Sibakhi or Sibahe" of the Assyrian records, who helped the king of Gaza, and says "This may be the person here spoken of." 2 Kings 17:4 [48]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
No other verse names So.
Scripture does not say whether So answered Hoshea or sent any help.
Scripture does not say where So reigned or for how long.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textScripture names So once, as "So king of Egypt" (2 Kgs 17:4). Who he was is disputed. The views below are those of writers up to 1915 whose words could be read for this page. Other identifications have been proposed since, among them Osorkon IV, Tefnakht, and reading "So" as the city of Sais rather than a king; the modern works that argue them could not be opened and checked, so they are not set out here. 2 Kings 17:4
